All active MLS® listings for detached houses in Sardis, BC appear on this page. Below, the local sub-areas are set side by side.
Sardis East Vedder
Sardis East Vedder: settled family streets on the east side of Vedder Road, near shops, parks and Sardis Secondary.
Sardis West Vedder
Sardis West Vedder: gated adult complexes and quiet cul-de-sacs on the west side of Vedder Road, close to the Vedder River trails.
Sardis South
Sardis South: the newer subdivisions and townhome sites that lead down to the Vedder River and Cultus Lake Road.
Promontory
Promontory: homes with hillside views and newer townhome complexes above Sardis, most built between 1995 and 2020.
Garrison Crossing
Garrison Crossing: on the site of the old CFB Chilliwack base, a walkable village of condos, townhomes and heritage-style homes.
Vedder Crossing
Vedder Crossing: the south side's commercial centre, where condos and townhomes sit near the Vedder River.

Most detached lots carry R1-A, R1-B or R1-C zoning (single detached), and under the City's small-scale multi-unit housing rules many can now have a secondary suite or coach house. Before you plan a suite, look at the City of Chilliwack zoning map and see whether title carries any restrictive covenants.

Floodplain: lower Sardis, Fairfield Island, Greendale, Rosedale and Yarrow include areas inside the Fraser and Vedder River floodplain, with the City's dike network providing protection. Find out the flood construction level for the property, what the lender and insurer require, and if a geotechnical or floodplain covenant has been registered on title.

Schools and transit: School District 33 (SD33) serves Chilliwack. Schools include Chilliwack Secondary, G.W. Graham Middle-Secondary and Sardis Secondary, with elementary catchments such as Unsworth, Watson and Vedder. Check the catchment with SD33 before you buy. For transit, BC Transit routes in Chilliwack follow Young Road, Luckakuck Way and Vedder Road, while the Fraser Valley Express (Route 66) connects Chilliwack with Abbotsford and with Carvolth Exchange in Langley.

Where are detached houses for sale in Sardis usually located?

Detached houses in Sardis are mostly found in Vedder Crossing, Garrison Crossing, Promontory, Sardis South, Sardis West Vedder and Sardis East Vedder. Age, lot size and price differ from area to area, so I suggest narrowing it to two or three neighbourhoods before booking showings.
How often do these Sardis house listings update?
Listings on this page update directly from the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board MLS® feed several times a day, so new listings, price changes and sold statuses appear quickly.
Before buying a Sardis house, what should I look into on zoning, strata or ALR?

Expect R1-A, R1-B or R1-C zoning (single detached) on most detached lots. Many of those now permit a secondary suite or coach house because of the City's small-scale multi-unit housing rules. Review the City of Chilliwack zoning map and restrictive covenants on title before deciding to add a suite.
Are any Sardis detached houses in the floodplain?

Some areas in Rosedale, Yarrow, Greendale, Fairfield Island and lower Sardis sit in the floodplain of the Fraser and Vedder Rivers, and the City's dike network protects them. Ask for the property's flood construction level and for the requirements of lenders and insurers, and check title for a registered geotechnical or floodplain covenant.
Which schools serve Sardis detached houses?

School District 33 (SD33) covers Chilliwack. Sardis Secondary and G.W. Graham take students from Sardis and the south side, and Chilliwack Secondary draws from the north side. Because catchments shift, check a particular address with SD33.
Is public transit available near Sardis detached houses?

Yes. The Fraser Valley Express goes to Abbotsford and Langley, and local BC Transit routes in Chilliwack run along Luckakuck Way, Young Road and Vedder Road. Bus service is thin or absent in rural areas like Ryder Lake, Greendale and Columbia Valley.
